descriptor.scene: A close, reverent study of one exhibited door in the hall: the plain honey-brown door hung flat on the cream museum wall in its simple wooden frame, a soft spotlight pooling on it from above, a low velvet rope on two brass stanchions in front. On the wall beside the frame, a small brass plaque with designed lettering that is fully legible and reads exactly "THE CLOUD", and nothing else. The frame, plaque, rope and light all sit beside or below the door and never touch its face. Keep the bottom right calm. The door leaf has EXACTLY FOUR recessed panels in TWO rows and no more: a top row of two small square panels, and below it a single row of two tall rectangular panels that reach nearly to the floor with only a plain flat rail beneath them. There is NO third row of panels at the bottom of the door.
negatives: any lettering other than the quoted plaque string
lettering on the door face itself
a six-panel colonial door, a third row of panels at the bottom of the door leaf
descriptor._caption: Each door has a frame, a spotlight, and a small brass plaque. Standing here, you would think nobody could have missed them.
